title: Integral finite-Tor-amplitude complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with characteristic $p$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible; put $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete bounded constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], a triangulated subcategory [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ let $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ be its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Let $P$ be the property of $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$: $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] for every $j\geq1$. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[m]$ does, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.46.4 (Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude), part (2), applied to the reductions, which carry distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ to distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ and commute with shifts; the integral category follows the blueprint node def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude.md)

proof.text: For each $j\geq1$ write $R_j(K)=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$. By the derived-reduction definition this is change of rings along $\pi_j:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,j})_Y$. Apply the exact derived-change-of-rings functor to this morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on the same site. Thus $R_j$ preserves distinguished triangles, zero objects and isomorphisms, and has the shift comparison $R_j(K[m])\cong R_j(K)[m]$. If $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, every $R_j(K)$ is bounded constructible by the integral-category definition. All finite-stage applications below are consequently on the small pro-etale site, with coefficient ring $A_{E,j}$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, label lemma-derived-base-change, applied to the identity of the site and the coefficient projection

proof.text: Isomorphism invariance: if $K\cong L$ and $P(K)$ holds, the integral constructible triangulated-subcategory lemma gives $L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. For every $j$ the reduction isomorphism $R_j(K)\cong R_j(L)$ induces, after derived tensor with any degree-zero $A_{E,j}$-module sheaf $N$, isomorphisms on cohomology. The same reasoning applies to any isomorphism between two objects of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$, so Tor amplitude in a specified interval is invariant under such an isomorphism. Therefore the same uniform interval $[a,b]$ works for $L$. For the zero object, the integral subcategory contains zero, and $R_j(0)$ is zero. Derived tensor of zero with any $N$ is computed by the zero K-flat complex and is zero, so $[0,0]$ works simultaneously for all $j$.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, label definition-tor-amplitude, and the zero complex in the derived-tensor construction

proof.text: Let $P(K)$ have uniform Tor interval $[a,b]$, and fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. The integral constructible subcategory contains $K[m]$. For each $j\geq1$, specialize [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated] with the same prime $\ell$, extension $E$, valuation ring and uniformizer, scheme $Y$, and $n=j$. Its coefficient ring is exactly $A_{E,j}$; the finite-stage statement explicitly binds these coefficient data to the coefficient-extension definition. Every $R_j(K)$ is bounded constructible by step 1 and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ by $P(K)$, so the explicit shift clause of the finite-stage triangulated lemma gives Tor amplitude $[a-m,b-m]$ for $R_j(K)[m]$. The comparison in step 1 and isomorphism invariance in step 2 give the same interval for $R_j(K[m])$, independently of $j$. Thus $P(K[m])$. Conversely apply this implication with $-m$ to $K[m]$ and use $(K[m])[-m]\cong K$ and step 2.

source.place: Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude, translation, as recorded with its interval in lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated

proof.text: Let $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ be distinguished, with $P(K)$ and $P(M)$. Choose their uniform Tor intervals $[a_K,b_K]$ and $[a_M,b_M]$ and put $a=\min(a_K,a_M)$ and $b=\max(b_K,b_M)$. Then $a\leq b$. For every $j$ and every degree-zero $A_{E,j}$-module sheaf $N$, an integer outside $[a,b]$ is outside each original interval, so the defining tensor cohomology vanishes for both $R_j(K)$ and $R_j(M)$. Both therefore have Tor amplitude in the common interval $[a,b]$, which is independent of $j$.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, label definition-tor-amplitude: enlarging the interval

proof.text: The integral constructible triangulated-subcategory lemma gives $L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. For each $j$, step 1 gives the distinguished triangle $R_j(K)\to R_j(L)\to R_j(M)\to R_j(K)[1]$. Its outside vertices are bounded constructible and have the common Tor interval of step 4. Apply the explicit extension clause of the finite-stage triangulated lemma, with the same $\ell,E,Y$ and $n=j\geq1$, in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$: $R_j(L)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Since neither endpoint of this interval depends on $j$, this proves $P(L)$.

source.place: Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude, part (2), for each reduced distinguished triangle

proof.text: Take the full subcategory on the objects satisfying $P$. Step 2 supplies isomorphism closure and zero; step 3 supplies closure under every integer shift (in both directions); steps 4-5 supply extension closure in distinguished triangles. These are precisely the conditions in the definition of a full triangulated subcategory, so this subcategory has the asserted triangulation inherited from the ambient derived category.
